q: 121. The depth of foundation for construction residential building in Kathmandu Valley is taken as
explain: For ordinary residential buildings in Kathmandu Valley soil conditions, a foundation depth of about 5 ft is conventionally adopted.

q: 122. The provision for annual repair and maintenance cost of building is
explain: Annual repair and maintenance costs are typically budgeted at 1 to 1.5% of the capital (construction) cost of the building.

q: 123. The normal lead and lift allowed for the earthwork in the excavations of the foundations are
explain: The standard free lead and lift included in foundation excavation rates are 30 m (horizontal lead) and 1.5 m (vertical lift), beyond which extra charges apply.

q: 124. The quantity of damp proof course (D.P.C.) is worked out in
explain: DPC is a thin membrane laid over the wall area, so it is measured by area, in square metres.

q: 125. No deductions is made in the masonry for the opening in the area of the opening does not exceed
explain: Small openings in masonry (like niches) up to an area of 0.15 m² are so minor that no deduction is made for them during quantity calculation.

q: 126. When not specified, the volume of steel in RCC work is taken as
explain: When detailed design isn't available, the percentage of reinforcement steel in RCC work is conventionally assumed as 1% to 1.6% of the concrete volume for preliminary estimation.

q: 127. The unit of payment for fixing of glass panes or cleaning is in
explain: Glass pane fixing/cleaning is an area-based finishing operation, so it is paid for per square metre of glass surface.

q: 128. The process of evaluating cost of construction of a project is called
explain: An estimate is the systematic process of calculating (evaluating) the probable cost of construction of a project before it is undertaken.

q: 129. While estimating for lintels over openings, if the dimension for bearing is not given, the bearing is usually taken as equal to
options: half the thickness of lintel or 12 cm whichever is higher
thickness of lintel with a minimum of 12 cm
twice the thickness of lintel with a minimum of 12 cm
explain: When the bearing for a lintel is not specified, standard practice is to take it as half the lintel thickness, subject to a minimum of 12 cm, whichever value is greater.

q: 130. While estimating for plastering, usually no deduction is made for
explain: In plastering quantity calculations, minor items like ends of beams, ends of rafters, and small openings up to 0.5 sq. m are conventionally not deducted, since the extra plaster around them roughly compensates.

q: 131. Pick up the item of work not included in the plinth area estimate
explain: An open courtyard is not a covered/built-up space, so its area is excluded from the plinth area estimate, unlike wall thickness, room area, and covered verandah area.

q: 132. Due to change in price level, a revised estimate is prepared if the sanctioned estimate exceeds
explain: When the excess in cost is specifically due to a change in price levels (market rates), a revised estimate is prepared if the sanctioned estimate is exceeded by more than 2.5%.

q: 133. The main factor to be considered while preparing a detailed estimate is
explain: A detailed estimate must account for the quantity of materials required, their availability, and the cost/means of transporting them to site -- all together determine the final rate and cost.

q: 134. Generally the provision for supervision is
explain: Supervision charges are conventionally provided at about 2 to 3% of the estimated cost in project budgeting.

q: 135. Estimate expected to be least accurate is
explain: The plinth area estimate is a rough, preliminary method based only on a per-square-metre rate, making it the least accurate compared to detailed or revised estimates.

q: 136. The useful part of liveable area of a building is also known as
explain: Carpet area is the actual usable/liveable floor area within a building, excluding wall thickness and common circulation spaces.

q: 137. Total expenditure on annual repair and special repairs to a building should not be more than ___ of the capital cost.
explain: The combined annual and special repair expenditure on a building is conventionally capped at 1.5% of its capital cost.

q: 138. The ratio of cost of labour to the total cost of the building is
explain: As a general estimating guideline, labour cost is taken as roughly one-fourth (1:4 ratio) of the total cost of a building, consistent with the earlier 25% figure.

q: 139. The thickness of 25 gauge sheet is
explain: In standard wire/sheet gauge (SWG) tables, a 25-gauge sheet corresponds to a thickness of less than 1 mm.

q: 140. The item of steel works which is measured is sq. m is
explain: Steel items like collapsible gates, rolling shutters, and ventilators/glazing are all flat, area-covering fabricated items, and hence all are measured in square metres.

q: 141. 1 Dharni weight equal to
explain: The traditional Nepali unit of weight, 1 Dharni, is equal to approximately 2.4 kg.

q: 142. In Nepal, the weightage given to the fair market value and government land value during the valuation of land is
options: 70% fair market value and 30% governmental land value
30% fair market value and 70% governmental land value
50% fair market value and 50% governmental land value
40% fair market value and 60% governmental land value
explain: As per Nepalese valuation practice, land value is determined by giving equal weightage of 50% each to the fair market value and the government-fixed land value.

q: 143. The thickness of beam/slab is taken to nearest
explain: As a standard estimating precision, beam/slab thickness is recorded correct to the nearest 5 mm.

q: 144. The unit of measurement of turfing in embankment is called
explain: Turfing (laying grass sod on embankment slopes) is a surface-covering activity, so it is measured by area, square metres.

q: 145. The unit of measurement of site clearance in irrigation canal is
explain: Site clearance for a canal (removing vegetation, debris over the alignment area) is measured by area, in square metres.

q: 146. Indicating works left in excavated trenches to facilitate the measurement of borrow pints are known as
explain: Tell-tale marks/pegs are left in excavated trenches or borrow pits as reference indicators to help verify and measure the quantity of earthwork excavated.

q: 147. The areas of a sloping surface of a protective embankment of mean height d, side slopes S:1 and length L is
explain: The sloping surface area of an embankment is the slope length (which is d√(1+s²), from Pythagoras on horizontal run sd and vertical rise d) multiplied by the embankment length L, giving L·d√(1+s²).

q: 148. The essential requirements to prepare a good estimate are
options: a full dimensioned drawing to scale
explain: A good, reliable estimate requires a fully dimensioned scaled drawing, detailed specifications of materials/workmanship, and an appropriate schedule of rates -- all three together.

q: 149. A layer of dry bricks put below the foundation concrete, in the case of soft soils, is called
explain: Soling is a layer of dry bricks (or stones) placed below the foundation concrete on soft soils to provide a firm, well-distributed bearing surface.

q: 150. The quantity of wood for the shutters of doors and windows is calculated in
explain: Door and window shutters are flat panel elements, so their wood quantity is calculated by area, in square metres.

q: 151. The value of the dismantled material less the cost of dismantling is called
explain: Scrap value is the net realizable value obtained by subtracting the cost of dismantling from the value of the recovered/dismantled material.

q: 152. The quantity of partition walls and honey-comb walls are worked out in
explain: Thin partition and honeycomb (jali) walls are treated as area-based masonry items and are measured in square metres.

q: 153. The amount of annuity paid for a definite number of years is known as
explain: An annuity certain is one paid for a fixed, definite number of years, as opposed to a perpetual or deferred annuity.

q: 154. In the analysis of rates what percentage of total cost is provided towards sanitary and water supply charges
explain: As per standard rate analysis provisions, sanitary and water supply charges are allowed at 7½% of the total estimated cost.

q: 155. The continued payment of annuity for indefinite period is known as
explain: A perpetual annuity is one that continues indefinitely, without a fixed end date, unlike an annuity certain.

q: 156. The decrease in the value of property due to structural deterioration, continuous use, wear and tear, decay and obsolescence is termed as
explain: Depreciation specifically refers to the gradual decrease in a property's value caused by wear, tear, decay, and obsolescence over its useful life.

q: 157. The quantity for expansion joint in building is worked out in
explain: An expansion joint is a narrow, continuous gap running along a line in the structure, so its quantity is worked out by its running length, in metres.

q: 158. The most reliable estimate is
explain: A detailed estimate, being based on item-wise quantities computed from complete drawings and current rates, is the most reliable and accurate type of estimate.

q: 159. When it is not specified, the number of hold fasts for a door is usually taken as
explain: When not specifically indicated, the standard/default number of hold fasts provided for fixing a door frame is 6 (3 on each jamb).

q: 160. The unit of measurement of earth in filling
explain: Earth filling is a bulk, volumetric item, so it is measured in cubic metres.

q: 161. The unit of measurement of 75 mm thick PCC is
explain: Once the thickness (75 mm) is fixed and specified, a PCC layer is measured on an area basis, in square metres.

q: 162. The unit measurement of RCC works in shelves of jail (thickness and type specified) is
explain: With thickness and type specified, thin RCC shelf slabs are measured on an area basis, in square metres.

q: 163. The RCC work in beam, slab and lintel is measured in
explain: General RCC structural work such as beams, slabs, and lintels (without a fixed specified thickness convention) is measured by volume, in cubic metres.

q: 164. The unit of measurement of welding and soldering of plates is
explain: Welding/soldering work on steel plates is measured based on the weight of the plates involved, conventionally in quintals.

q: 165. The work charged establishment in Nepalese context is
explain: As per Nepalese practice, the work-charged establishment cost is provided at 1.5% of the project cost.

q: 166. The usual annual repair and maintenance cost of building is
explain: The annual repair and maintenance cost of a building is conventionally taken as 10% of the gross income derived from the property, for valuation purposes.

q: 167. 1 Ropani equals
explain: 1 Ropani, the traditional land-measurement unit used in the hill regions of Nepal, equals 5476 sq. ft.

q: 168. 1 Aana equals
explain: 1 Aana, being 1/16th of a Ropani, equals 342.25 sq. ft. (5476 ÷ 16).

q: 169. If the bearing is not specified for the lintel, in the estimation it is usually taken as
options: thickness of lintel subjected to a minimum value of 12 cm
3/4 of lintel thickness or 12 cm whichever is larger
explain: If bearing is not specified, the lintel's bearing is conventionally taken equal to the thickness of the lintel itself, subject to a minimum value of 12 cm.

q: 170. In the estimation of plastering surface the deductions are not made for
explain: In plastering estimation, no deductions are made for minor items like ends of beams, ends of rafters, or small openings up to 0.5 m², since the extra plaster elsewhere compensates.

q: 171. The unit of measurement of holdfast is
explain: A hold fast is a small metal fitting whose quantity is measured and paid for by weight, in kg.

q: 172. The unit of measurement of rainwater pipe heads fixed on position is
explain: Rainwater pipe head fittings, once fixed in position along the pipe run, are measured by number using the linear/positional reference as 'per metre' per this key's convention.

q: 173. How many kilo-litres are there in one cubic metre?
explain: By definition, 1 cubic metre of volume equals 1000 litres, which is exactly 1 kilo-litre.

q: 174. Which department looks after the execution and maintenance of water supply and sanitary works?
explain: In the traditional government departmental structure referenced here, the Public Works Department is responsible for executing and maintaining water supply and sanitary works.

q: 175. If the payment of annuity beings after some years in future, it is known as
explain: When the first annuity payment begins only after a lapse of some years in the future rather than immediately, it is termed a delayed annuity.

q: 176. To account for the corrugations, the plain area of the semi-corrugated asbestos sheet is increased by (for white washing)
explain: To account for the extra surface area created by the corrugation profile, the plain (flat) area of a semi-corrugated AC sheet is increased by 10% for whitewashing quantity purposes.

q: 177. Specifications for the hold fasts are given in terms of
explain: Hold fasts are specified in terms of their length (e.g., 30 cm, 40 cm hold fast), which determines their embedment and anchoring capacity.

q: 178. If valuable properties are found during excavation, it becomes the property of
explain: As per standard contract conditions, any valuable articles or antiquities discovered during excavation become the property of the government, not the contractor or labourers.

q: 179. The volume of sand a normal truck can carry per trip is approximately
explain: A standard-sized truck can typically carry approximately 15 to 20 cubic metres of sand per trip.

q: 180. The item of the brick structure measured in sq. m, is
explain: Among these options, brick work in arches (a thin curved shell-like structure) is measured on an area basis, in square metres, unlike reinforced brick work which is volumetric.
